![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227606/assets/2c9f6bba4d2a0e1b1499a8813a2035f838113cbcb5e0fe20c219f45bf011c471.png)

Solve for $x$ in the figure above given that $\overset{⟷}{PQ}$ is the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{MN}.$
q-52978.worked_solution:
By the perpendicular bisector theorem, a point on the perpendicular bisector of a segment is equidistant from the endpoints of the segment. Hence, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}QM & =QN \\ 2x-3 & =3x-10 \\ -3 & =x-10 \\ 7 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

q-53023.name: Question 2
q-53023.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227606/assets/fae19bb8db103c78bf70bfb65d807f18df344264606282c7a56392a659012f8a.png)

Solve for $x$ in the figure above given that $VY=WY$ and $VZ=WZ.$
q-53023.worked_solution:
By the converse of the perpendicular bisector theorem, a point equidistant from the endpoints of a segment lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment.

Here, the points $Y$ and $Z$ are both equidistant from the endpoints of $\overset{―}{VW}.$ Therefore, $Y$ and $Z$ both  lie on the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{VW}.$    

Since only one line can be drawn through two given points, the line $\overset{⟷}{YZ}$ is the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{VW}.$ 

In particular, we have that $VX=WX.$ We can use this equation to solve for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}VX & =WX \\ 4x-2 & =2x+4 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

q-76794.worked_solution:
By the converse of the perpendicular bisector theorem, a point equidistant from the endpoints of a segment lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment. 

Here, the points $P$ and $N$ are both equidistant from the endpoints of $\overset{―}{KL}.$ Therefore, $P$ and $N$ both  lie on the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{KL}.$ 

Since only one line can be drawn through two given points, the line $\overset{⟷}{PN}$ is the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{KL}.$ 

In particular, we have that $KM=LM.$ We can use this equation to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}KM & =LM \\ 2x+2 & =4x-6 \\ -2x & =-8 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$
